misconception_description: Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.

solutions.generated_code:
program HitungProduk
kamus
  a, b, hasil, count : integer
algoritma
  input(a, b)
  hasil <- 0
  count <- 0
  if count < b then
    hasil <- hasil + a
    count <- count + 1
  endif
  output(hasil)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student attempts to compute the product by repeated addition (a * b = adding a to itself b times). They use an if-statement with a counter, believing it will execute repeatedly until count reaches b, similar to how a while loop would work. In reality, the if-statement only executes once, so the function returns a instead of a * b. From the student's perspective, this should correctly compute the product because they believe the if-statement will keep running as long as count < b, incrementing the counter and accumulating the sum until the condition becomes false.
